snippets.output: Anal fissures and hemorrhoids have different healing outcomes depending on the severity and treatment methods employed.

Acute anal fissures can often heal on their own with conservative management, which includes dietary modification (a high-fiber diet), adequate hydration, and stool softeners to reduce strain during defecation.

Chronic anal fissures are less likely to heal without medical intervention and may require treatments such as topical nitrates, calcium channel blockers, or surgical options like lateral internal sphincterotomy, which has a high success rate for healing chronic fissures.

Mild cases of internal hemorrhoids can resolve on their own with conservative measures such as a high-fiber diet, increased fluid intake, and over-the-counter treatments including topical agents and sitz baths.
Severe cases of internal hemorrhoids (grade III and IV) often require procedural interventions such as rubber band ligation, sclerotherapy, or surgical hemorrhoidectomy.

External hemorrhoids can also often resolve on their own (especially if not thrombosed) with conservative measures similar to those used for internal hemorrhoids; thrombosed external hemorrhoids, however, can be very painful and may require medical procedures for relief.
